A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ImageNot study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNot training experiments, CIFAR10 fine-tuning and transfer results, dataset analyses, and corruption experiments, including Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments with nine architectures, CIFAR10 transfer evaluations, corruption results, and a new ImageNet-versus-ImageNot discrimination experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3 revises the final dataset-construction step: v1 ranks classes by caption–synset-gloss similarity using RoBERTa, whereas v2 selects them by average similarity of the top 1100 class–image pairs using CLIP, also shown in Figure 3. This is a localized change to the reported selection procedure; the preceding filtering stages remain.

E1.justification: ImageNet, ImageNot, CIFAR10, and the 17 corruption types remain. V2 adds binary dataset-origin classification—distinguishing ImageNet images from ImageNot images—in Section 3.1 and Figure 7. This adds a distinct task using existing data sources.

E2.justification: The evaluated architecture set expands from six to nine, adding Inception V3, MobileNet V3 Large, and ViT-B/16 to the ranking and downstream comparisons. Figures 1, 8, and 9 in v2 verify their participation. ViT was cited but not evaluated in v1; ResNet18's textual mention in v1 does not establish an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V1 reports a shared, four-configuration ImageNot search with SGD and restricted tuning. V2 instead specifies architecture-specific reference recipes, including different optimizers, batch sizes, schedules, and augmentation or regularization such as mixup, cutmix, and label smoothing (Appendix A.1). It also introduces the dataset-discrimination sample-size protocol and changes the principal regression from raw to relative accuracies. These are reported protocol revisions, beyond additional documentation.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of dataset distinguishability and its sensitivity to training-set size, from 100 to one million images per dataset (Figure 7). Conversely, v1's separate corruption-by-corruption ranking analyses for ImageNet, ImageNot, and CIFAR10 (Appendix B.2, Figures 10–12) are removed. Aggregate corruption comparisons remain, so the detailed robustness evidence is lost rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: The new discrimination experiment reports error bars over three trials with fresh data sampling and model initialization. Both versions already report three CIFAR10 restarts, standard errors, and 95% regression confidence intervals. V2 therefore adds uncertainty information for a new experiment without establishing an increased repeat count for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 replaces and expands the main result series under revised training: the reported best ImageNot accuracy changes from approximately 50% to 60%. It adds 97.0% dataset-discrimination accuracy and replaces the raw-accuracy fit (slope 0.46, adjusted R-squared 0.98) with a relative-accuracy fit (slope 1.01, Pearson R 0.99). It also reports ConvNeXt outperforming EfficientNet V2 under averaged corruptions. Changed settings and metrics prevent interpreting these differences as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Neither version develops original theorems or proofs. The WordNet concepts and relative-progress definition remain unchanged. V2's citation of a theoretical study and reporting of standard correlation statistics do not introduce new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The central ranking-preservation claim remains. V2's abstract focuses on training from scratch and drops the claim of similar transfer-learning utility. The introduction explicitly presents ImageNot as a test of scientific progress rather than a replacement benchmark. The conclusion also removes v1's unbiased-noise qualification from the claim that clean labels may be unnecessary.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly separates benchmarking equivalence from pretraining usefulness, concluding that ImageNet is superior for pretraining. It clarifies that ImageNot's noise includes natural image variability as well as incorrect labels, and limits applicability to benchmarking scientific progress. V1's explanation attributing corruption-specific instability to restricted tuning disappears with the detailed appendix discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds extensive per-model ImageNot recipes and a compute table specifying A100 resources and GPU-hours. However, v2 omits v1's explicit four-run ImageNot budget and CIFAR10 batch-size exceptions. The code destination remains the same. V2 removes the statement that images and URLs are not released, but does not document an actual release.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially revise the positioning: earlier ranking studies are characterized as establishing internal validity, five confounds are identified, and the comparison with Kornblith et al.'s training-from-scratch experiments is developed. Added references include ObjectNet, Liu and He (2024), and Dorner and Hardt (2024), alongside the newly evaluated architectures. This changes the novelty argument beyond citation expansion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work narrative, and experimental discussion receive extensive rewriting. Related work gains thematic paragraph headings, the conclusion loses its extended future-work discussion, and the appendices are reorganized around ImageNot recipes, CIFAR10 settings, robustness procedures, and additional results. These changes substantially alter the narrative independently of new experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds image examples, a curation flowchart, and the discrimination plot; redraws rankings for nine models; and restructures the transfer plots. Dataset-distribution and WordNet figures move to the appendix, while detailed corruption-ranking figures disappear. The default-hyperparameter table is replaced by a compute table. The new example figure also has a caption that reverses the displayed left/right dataset order.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's six-model study, v2 provides broader architectural evidence, including a transformer, a direct dataset-distinguishability test, clearer pretraining limitations, and more reproducibility information. These strengthen the paper's support and auditability. However, detailed corruption evidence is removed, and the revised CLIP-based selection rule conflicts with retained claims of caption-only selection. These tradeoffs limit the net quality gain despite the extensive revision.
